outline: Disorders of the liver and biliary system, noninfectious
OATP1B1/OATP1B3-mediated hepatic uptake and reuptake of conjugated bilirubin
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Rotor syndrome results from combined loss of the sinusoidal organic anion transporters OATP1B1 and OATP1B3, encoded by SLCO1B1 and SLCO1B3. Impaired hepatic uptake/reuptake of conjugated bilirubin from sinusoidal blood reduces hepatic storage and promotes predominantly conjugated hyperbilirubinemia without the dark hepatic pigment of Dubin-Johnson syndrome.
vignette: A 19-year-old man has intermittent scleral icterus that began in childhood. He feels well. Total bilirubin is elevated with a predominantly conjugated fraction, but aminotransferases, alkaline phosphatase, and albumin are normal. There is no evidence of hemolysis. Liver histology shows no coarse dark pigment. Genetic testing identifies loss of functional OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 transporters.
lead: Which of the following transport defects most directly explains this patient's hyperbilirubinemia?
correct: Impaired sinusoidal uptake and reuptake of conjugated bilirubin into hepatocytes
distractors: Impaired canalicular export of conjugated bilirubin through MRP2
Impaired canalicular export of bile acids through the bile salt export pump
Impaired incorporation of copper into ceruloplasmin with reduced biliary copper excretion
distractor_notes: MRP2 deficiency causes Dubin-Johnson syndrome, another benign conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, but it is a canalicular excretion defect and is associated with characteristic dark hepatic pigment.
UGT1A1 deficiency causes unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, as in Gilbert or Crigler-Najjar syndromes, not the predominantly conjugated pattern shown here.
Bile salt export pump defects cause cholestatic liver disease with impaired bile-acid secretion rather than isolated benign Rotor-type hyperbilirubinemia.
ATP7B dysfunction causes Wilson disease with abnormal copper handling and systemic copper accumulation, not isolated lifelong conjugated hyperbilirubinemia.
key_expl: This patient has Rotor syndrome. OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 are sinusoidal hepatocyte transporters that mediate uptake and reuptake of organic anions, including conjugated bilirubin. Combined deficiency interrupts hepatic reuptake of conjugated bilirubin and reduces hepatic storage, producing mild predominantly conjugated hyperbilirubinemia with otherwise normal liver function. Unlike Dubin-Johnson syndrome, Rotor syndrome does not produce coarse dark hepatic pigment because the defect is sinusoidal uptake/reuptake rather than MRP2-mediated canalicular secretion.
objective: Explain Rotor syndrome as loss of OATP1B1/OATP1B3-mediated sinusoidal hepatic uptake/reuptake of conjugated bilirubin.
